new_statements.quote: 彝语中的每个音节都有声调。但各地的声调数量多少不等,一般有3-5个声调。彝语南部方言双柏话有高平、中平、低降三个声调。彝语除了有声调外,有些音节还带有表意重音或表情重音。重音是相连的音节中某个音节发音突出的现象,它出现在句子中,同时也出现在某些语言的单词中。如云南双柏彝语: do2'love33 “得了!”或“够了!”(看见异常情况时所发出来的自然感叹声或紧急呼声)凉山彝语 … mo33 “阿妈!”(遇到危险时的惊呼声)这类摹描自然声响的象声词和叹词,都带表意重音或表情重音。另外,彝语的表意重音有区别词汇意义和语法意义的作用。
new_statements.translation: Every syllable in Yi carries a tone, though the number of tones varies from place to place, generally 3-5. The Shuangbai speech of the Southern dialect of Yi has three tones: high level, mid level and low falling. Besides tone, in Yi some syllables also carry sense-marking stress (表意重音) or expressive stress (表情重音). Stress is the phenomenon in which one syllable among connected syllables is pronounced prominently; it occurs in sentences and, in some languages, also within words. E.g. Yunnan Shuangbai Yi do21 lo33 've33 'That will do!'/'Enough!' (a spontaneous exclamation or urgent cry on seeing something unusual); Liangshan Yi ... mo33 'Mother!' (a cry of alarm in danger) - onomatopoeic words and interjections of this kind all carry sense-marking or expressive stress. In addition, the sense-marking stress of Yi serves to distinguish lexical meaning and grammatical meaning.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Shuangbai (E-Xin) Nisu is described as a syllable-tone language (every syllable bears one of three tones, 55/33/21) with no positional word-stress rule; instead the author recognises a marked, sporadic 'sense-marking stress' and 'expressive stress' borne by particular syllables (interjections, onomatopoeia, and elsewhere as a lexically/grammatically contrastive feature). Where such stress falls within a word is not stated in the accessible text.
new_statements.exceptions: Only that interjections/onomatopoeia carry expressive or sense-marking stress and that sense-marking stress can distinguish lexical and grammatical meaning; no positional statement or exceptions visible.
new_statements.domain_note: The passage is framed for 'Yi' in general with the author's own Shuangbai Southern-Yi datapoint as the example (plus a Liangshan Yi example); stress is said to occur 'in sentences and also in words'. Only snippet-level access: a later, fuller treatment of 表意重音 in the Shuangbai description proper (e.g. on demonstratives or reduplication) could exist but did not surface in any snippet query (mine or the ache1244 the compilers).
new_statements.identity_note: Target languoid: Glottolog nort2718 'Northwestern Nisu' = ISO yiv 'Northern Nisu' = Chen et al.'s E-Xin (Eshan-Xinping) Yi = Yang 2009's NW Nisu (Eshan, Xinping, Yimen, Jiangchuan, Hongta, Tonghai, Jinning, Shuangbai; autonym Nasu(pho) in Eshan, Nishu/Nyiesu in Xinping). The quoted source, Li Shengfu 1996, describes 双柏话 (Shuangbai county Nisu), which Li himself labels '南部方言峨新土语' (E-Xin vernacular) and which Yang 2009 p.15 explicitly uses as her evidence for NW Nisu - hence nort2718. Caveat: Glottolog 5.1's sources.bib files Li 1996 under farn1234 [nsf] 'Far Northwestern Nisu' (apparently equating Yang's 'NW Nisu' with the ISO name 'Northwestern Nisu' = Yongping/Yunlong Nisu); by content (Shuangbai, E-Xin) the datapoint belongs with nort2718, but the catalog should record the Shuangbai datapoint explicitly. The statement itself is framed pan-Yi with Shuangbai examples.

new_statements.translation: Every syllable in Yi has a tone, but the number of tones varies from place to place, generally 3-5. The Shuangbai speech of the Southern Yi dialect has three tones: high level, mid level and low falling. Besides having tones, some syllables in Yi also carry 'semantic stress' or 'expressive stress'. Stress is the phenomenon in which one syllable among adjacent syllables is pronounced prominently; it occurs in sentences and, in some languages, also within words. E.g. Yunnan Shuangbai Yi do21'lo ve33 'That's it!' / 'Enough!' (a spontaneous exclamation or urgent cry on seeing something abnormal); Liangshan Yi a33'mo33 'Mother!' (a cry of alarm in danger). Onomatopoeic words and interjections of this kind all carry semantic or expressive stress. In addition, semantic stress in Yi serves to distinguish lexical meaning and grammatical meaning.

new_statements.identity_note: Ache 阿车 (yif, ache1244) is an ethnonym-based ISO split (Bradley/Pelkey 2007) with zero descriptive references in Glottolog. Yunnan (1955:40) reports the Xinping Ache autonym as Nisu (nei33 su33 phɯ21) and their speech as ~93% lexically identical, grammar identical, to local Xinping Yi, i.e. Nisu/Southern Yi; Wang Chengyou (2003) lists 阿车 as an exonym of Nisu; NCPSSD ethnomusicology titles call the Damaidi (Shuangbai) Ache the 'Nisu branch'. The stress statement quoted is from Li Shengfu (1996), whose datapoint is '双柏话/双柏彝语' (Shuangbai Southern Yi) -- Yang (2009:15) files that datapoint as NW Northern Nisu (yiv, nort2718). Li's snippets never use the name 阿车, so the equation Li-1996-Shuangbai = Ache is probable (Shuangbai's Southern-dialect Yi are the Ache plus small Chesu/Shansu groups) but unconfirmed; the statement may equally belong under nort2718. an earlier compilation named source (Lama 2012) does not cover Ache at all: it describes Azhe 阿哲 of Mile (yiz, azhe1235), a different language that Ethnologue confusingly lists as an alternate name of Ache.

tone_statements.citation: Ye, Zehua 叶泽华. 2010. 新平彝语松紧嗓音研究 [A study of tense and lax phonation in Xinping Yi]. In 语音乐律研究报告 2010 (Status Report of Phonetic and Music Research 2010), 105-122. Beijing: 北京大学中文系语言学实验室 (Linguistics Lab, Dept. of Chinese, Peking University).
tone_statements.quote: 新平彝语共有 35 个声母，18 个韵母，3 个声调，有非常整齐的松紧音对立，音系如下：… 声调（3） 第一调 33 第二调 21 第三调 55 新平彝语 33 调和 21 调都存在松紧音对立，而 55 调没有，为方便起见，本文将 33、21 调与松紧音的搭配分别处理为两个声调。… 故本文将新平彝语声调系统一共处理为 5 个调位，即 33 松、33 紧、21 松、21 紧、55 松。
tone_statements.translation: Xinping Yi has 35 initials, 18 finals and 3 tones, with a very regular tense/lax opposition; the system is as follows: ... Tones (3): tone 1 = 33, tone 2 = 21, tone 3 = 55. In Xinping Yi the 33 and 21 tones both show the tense/lax opposition while the 55 tone does not; for convenience this paper treats the combinations of the 33 and 21 tones with tense and lax phonation as two tones each. ... Hence the Xinping Yi tone system is treated as 5 tonal categories in all: 33 lax, 33 tense, 21 lax, 21 tense, 55 lax.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.1 新平彝语音位系统, p. 109; abstract p. 105

tone_statements.citation: Shi, Feng 石锋. 2008. 语音格局——语音学与音系学的交汇点 [Sound patterns: the interface of phonetics and phonology]. Beijing: 商务印书馆 (Commercial Press). Chapter 5 '南部彝语松紧元音的声学表现'.
tone_statements.quote: 5.3 实验设计我们以新平县老厂乡竹园村的彝语为例,分析其中元音松紧的对立在声学上的表现。这种彝语属彝语南部方言,不同于 Maddison 和 Ladefoged 已经做过实验的北部的禄劝那苏彝语。虽然它们都有三个声调,可是禄劝那苏彝语
tone_statements.translation: 5.3 Experimental design. We take the Yi of Zhuyuan village, Laochang township, Xinping county as our example and analyse how its tense/lax vowel opposition is expressed acoustically. This Yi belongs to the Southern dialect of Yi, unlike the northern Luquan Nasu Yi on which Maddieson and Ladefoged experimented. Although both have three tones, Luquan Nasu Yi ...

tone_statements.citation: Zhou, Decai 周德才. 1998. 彝族与拉祜族的历史语言比较研究 [A historical-linguistic comparison of the Yi and the Lahu]. 贵州民族研究 Guizhou minzu yanjiu 1998(3): 144-149, 143.
tone_statements.quote: 二、语言的比较彝以滇南新平 me 33 su 55 “聂苏话”为代表,拉祜语是以澜沧拉祜纳为代表进行两种语言语音现象的比较和分析。彝语和拉祜语均属于彝语支语言,都有各自独立的语音系统。… 音分松紧和有声调。彝语和拉祜语的语音系统各自内部发展也具有不平衡性。
tone_statements.translation: II. Comparison of the languages. For Yi, the Niesu speech [ne33su55] of Xinping in southern Yunnan is taken as representative; for Lahu, Lancang Lahu Na; the phonetic phenomena of the two languages are compared and analysed. Yi and Lahu both belong to the Yi branch and each has its own independent sound system. ... [both have] vowels divided into tense and lax, and tones. The internal development of the Yi and Lahu sound systems is also uneven.

sources.quote: 新平彝语共有 35 个声母，18 个韵母，3 个声调，有非常整齐的松紧音对立，音系如下：… 声调（3） 第一调 33 第二调 21 第三调 55 新平彝语 33 调和 21 调都存在松紧音对立，而 55 调没有，为方便起见，本文将 33、21 调与松紧音的搭配分别处理为两个声调。… 故本文将新平彝语声调系统一共处理为 5 个调位，即 33 松、33 紧、21 松、21 紧、55 松。

sources.note: Sec. 2.1 gives the phoneme system: 35 initials, 18 finals, 3 tones (tone 1 = 33, tone 2 = 21, tone 3 = 55); tones 33 and 21 each occur with both tense and lax phonation, 55 only lax, so the author analyses 5 tone-register categories (33 lax, 33 tense, 21 lax, 21 tense, 55 lax) and builds EGG phonation profiles (F0, open quotient, speed quotient) per category for male and female speakers; abstract: F0 differs little between tense and lax categories, lax has clearly higher OQ and lower SQ; sec. 4.3-4.4 define distinctive F0/OQ/SQ features per tone and argue 'tense/lax' is a phonation-mode, not…

tone.translation: Xinping Yi has 35 initials, 18 finals and 3 tones, with a very regular tense/lax opposition; the system is as follows: ... Tones (3): tone 1 = 33, tone 2 = 21, tone 3 = 55. In Xinping Yi the 33 and 21 tones both show the tense/lax opposition while the 55 tone does not; for convenience this paper treats the combinations of the 33 and 21 tones with tense and lax phonation as two tones each. ... Hence the Xinping Yi tone system is treated as 5 tonal categories in all: 33 lax, 33 tense, 21 lax, 21 tense, 55 lax.

tone.translation: II. Comparison of the languages. For Yi, the Niesu speech [ne33su55] of Xinping in southern Yunnan is taken as representative; for Lahu, Lancang Lahu Na; the phonetic phenomena of the two languages are compared and analysed. Yi and Lahu both belong to the Yi branch and each has its own independent sound system. ... [both have] vowels divided into tense and lax, and tones. The internal development of the Yi and Lahu sound systems is also uneven.
